summary: Read all 10 religion records (record 29), the cell religion array (record 26) against cells' province (27), culture (19) and state (25), the 101 temple flags in burg_features.json, the sacred-forest markers, and every faith mention in the annals (146 events with faith words, checked by hand where flagged), the gazetteer (311 burgs mention a faith) and B_faiths.md. AGREE: all 9 faith names, types, forms, deities and cultures match B's table; lineage of the 7 Ròdaich faiths (origins [2], from the Old Spirits) and of the Old Spirits and Tuathach (roots of their own) matches B II; burg counts per faith match B exactly once the 5 moved burgs are fixed (126/9/14/133/103/21/86 (35 Ròdaich+51 Tuathaich)/12/1 = 505); town populations (Old Spirits 1.23 M, Unicorn 1.19 M 'close behind') match; every temple flag agrees with the faith of its town and the gazetteer (Cnoc naomh's ancestor-shrine is already explained in B VII); 306 of 311 gazetteer faith mentions agree and the other 5 are keyword false alarms. CONFLICTS (5 map, 3 history): (a) burg_moves.json moved 5 harbour towns onto cells of another faith, turning Baile ghlas and Seann Warr Scorpion and Ros chiar, Seann Toll and Baile shean Old Spirits, against B, world.json and the gazetteer: map edits restore each town's faith on its new cell; (b) 5 religion centres (Old Spirits, Deer, Unicorn, Wolf, Tuathach) sat away from the seats the history names: map edits move them to Dùn ìseal, Dùn thais, Cathair dhearg, Inis thais and Doire ghlas (Rite, Hawk, Scorpion and Grey Night centres already agree); (c) history: V-0165 called Caol shean the largest Deer town in the east (it is fourth), V-0219 placed the Wolf census in a shire that is three-fifths Scorpion, and Muileann naomh was a Hawk house in the annals but is a Rite town with a temple on the map (new event V-0030a joins them). MISSING (written in): each faith's shires (held/shared counts and names) and temples; the Grey Night's descent from the Scorpion (origins [3]); the faiths' reach (expansion culture/state/global and expansionism, summarised as which faiths seek converts); the 144 land cells with no faith (far north-western cape, most of it outside any shire, plus Eilean ghorm, Eilean dhubh and Eilean gheal) as land the census enters as gun chreideamh; the Deer's sacred wood standing in Old Spirits country; Allt an Àigh in Deer country; the Tuathach holy places (3 temples). NOISE not written: religion codes (KB, OM, Kn…) and colours.

event.title: The Scorpion's priests on the grey night
event.body: The Scorpion's priests at Ceann mhòr answer the Mission's report on the grey-night gatherings. The practice was learned from the Ròdaich, they say, but from their own harbours and not from Baile chrom: the human fishing families of Ceann mhòr learned the prayer to keep the sea shut from them, and the labourers inland keep it as a night of silence, praying to a grey goose instead of Cnut. The priests call it the Scorpion gone astray and do not admit its keepers to their house.

event.title: The hawk-house at Muileann naomh takes the order
event.body: The hawk-house at Muileann naomh, the southernmost of the Hawk's houses and the farthest from Cnoc bheag, accepts the Rite's written order of worship and becomes a house of Creideamh nan Ròdach. Its bell, the first hung in a hawk-house, is rung now at the Rite's measured burnings. No other house of the Hawk follows it.

event.title: The census of the faiths
event.body: The first census of the restored kingdom enters every town under the faith its people keep, the first such roll since Seumas Bàn's clerks counted the rites at Dùn ìseal. On the far north-western cape beyond Baile chrom, where there is no town, the clerks find scattered families with no house of any faith, and on Eilean ghorm and the smallest islets no one to ask. They enter all of it as *gun chreideamh*, without a faith.

'The Wolf shires of the south-west': Inis thais' shire (15) is three-fifths Scorpion land; Doire shean's (10) is wholly Wolf and holds the faith's largest town.

gazetteer_edit.new: Its hawk-house was the southernmost of Creideamh an t-Seabhaig, the first on Rodos to hang a bronze bell, until it took the Rite's written order in the first years of the restored kingdom; the bell now rings for the Rite.
The Scorpion's priests at Ceann mhòr hold that the Grey Night grew out of their own prayer to keep the sea shut, and call it the Scorpion gone astray.
Its first human fishing families learned the Scorpion's harbour prayers here, and its priests say the Grey Night of Baile chrom began from them.

text_edit.old: That is not a mistake in the count, and section XII explains it.
text_edit.new:
That is not a mistake in the count, and section XII explains it.

**Shires and temples.** Counted by land rather than by towns, the faiths divide the island's 123 shires as follows. A faith *holds* a shire where it has more of the shire's land than any other faith, and *shares* one where it has a smaller part. The temples are the houses the map marks as temples.

| Faith | Shires held | Shires shared | Temples |
|---|---|---|---|
| Seann Spioradan nan Ròdach | 34 | 11 | 24 |
| Creideamh nan Ròdach | 4 | 1 | 5 |
| Creideamh an t-Seabhaig | 4 | 1 | 8 |
| Feallsanachd an Fhèidh | 23 | 10 | 16 |
| Creideamh an Aon-adharcaich Dhuibh | 29 | 5 | 17 |
| Creideamh a' Mhadaidh-allaidh | 8 | 4 | 8 |
| Creideamh na Scairpe Buidhe | 15 | 7 | 19 |
| Creideamh nan Tuathach | 3 | 6 | 3 |
| Rùn-dìomhair na h-Oidhche Glaise | 1 | 1 | 1 |

That accounts for 121 shires. In the other two no faith has the greater part. In {{place:province:90}} in the south-east the Old Spirits, the Rite and the Dark Unicorn have almost equal shares and the Deer a small one. In {{place:province:120}}, the shire whose lands take in the far north-western cape, most of the land keeps no faith at all.

**Descent.** The Old Spirits are the old reverence itself, kept at the hearths without a break, and they descend from nothing older that the record can name. The Obsidian Rite, the Hawk, the Deer, the Dark Unicorn, the Wolf and the Yellow Scorpion all grew out of it, as the companies of the Hall's council at the end of the Holy Age (section II). The Faith of the Tuathaich has its own root, which the record cannot trace. The Mystery of the Grey Night is the only faith on Rodos that grew out of another organised faith: it came out of the Yellow Scorpion (section XI).

**How they spread.** Four faiths have never sought converts beyond their own people: the Old Spirits, the Rite, the Hawk and the Faith of the Tuathaich. Each is held where its people live and nowhere else. The Deer and the Dark Unicorn spread with the kingdom, the one through its schools and the other through the crown's favour, and neither has gone beyond the Ròdaich. Since King Aonghas took it up, the Unicorn has spread faster than any other faith. The Yellow Scorpion, the Wolf and the Grey Night take in anyone of any people who comes to them. Only the Scorpion has won a second people. The Wolf, for all its open doors, is still held only in Ròdaich towns of the south-west.

**Land without a faith.** No faith holds the far north-western cape beyond Baile chrom. It has no town, and most of it lies outside any shire. Its few families, herders and shore-folk, most of them Tuathaich, have no house of any faith, and the first census of the restored kingdom entered them as *gun chreideamh*, without a faith ({{date:V-0034a}}). The same entry covers Eilean ghorm, where the grey geese winter and are never hunted ({{date:I-0055}}), Eilean dhubh, where the sea-thieves' boats were burned ({{date:III-0133}}), and the islet of Eilean gheal off the south-east coast. The cape has been thinly held since the dearth on the north-west shore ({{date:III-0134}}).
text_edit.why: Shires held/shared per faith computed from the map's cell religion and province arrays; the faiths' lineage (origins), expansion type and the land with no faith (Gun chreideamh, 144 land cells) were in the map and not in the history.

unsure: Rebuild safety: burg_features.py / burg_moves.json move burgs but leave the cells' religion array alone, so a rebuild from Rodos_renamed.map would put the 5 moved towns back on the wrong faith. Whoever applies this should add the religion fix to the move step (carry the old cell's religion to the new cell) or apply these record-26 edits after burg_features.apply(). The same goes for the Atlas copy Rodos_Atlas/Rodos.map (identical to Rodos_finished.map today) and world.json (its 'faith' field already has the pre-move faiths, which is what these edits restore).

If a one-cell enclave is unwanted, drop that edit and change B's counts to Old Spirits 127 / Deer 132 instead (nothing in the history names Seann Toll's faith).

Province 120 'Seann Vell' is broken on the map: its seat Seann Vell (burg 127) is one cell on the south-west coast, and the rest of its land is the far north-western cape (no faith / Tuathach) plus an 8-cell Old Spirits pocket in the south at x≈735, y≈500. For the provinces layer. B refers to it only as 'the shire whose lands take in the far north-western cape'.

The 81 no-faith cells with no province are state 0 (Neutrals) on the map. B says only that 'most of it lies outside any shire'; if the states layer writes the cape into the kingdom or out of it, the Land without a faith paragraph may need one more clause.
Provinces 122 'Siorrachd fhionn' and 123 'Siorrachd àrsaidh' have no seat burg and doubled names; B cites 122 by its token only. For the provinces layer.

Record 29 field 'center' in FMG is the cell the religion radiates from; I used it for the faith's seat, which is what B's table calls the seat. Expansion/expansionism values were left as generated and described in prose.

IV-0262a and V-0030a add small new facts (the Scorpion priests' view of the Grey Night; Muileann naomh's change of house). They fill gaps the record left open and contradict nothing, but B XI no longer says the Grey Night's source is unknown.
